evidence.note: CONFIRMED: baseline_red.on_base builds todo as [i for i in ids if i not in known or (known.get(i) and (i not in cached_sigs or len(cached_sigs[i]) == LINE_CHARS))], so any cached base signature exactly LINE_CHARS long is re-measured on EVERY gate run. A genuinely-whole reason of exactly 240 chars is indistinguishable from a legacy cut-to-240 entry, so it is redundantly re-run (the bug). Verified by reading the code at ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:100-105 and flakes.LINE_CHARS=240; ruby_demo: cache_store(cut==240) then on_base -> todo non-empty.
Followed work-queue rules: claimed, regression test first, cross-family review, scoped unit_tests before merge, regression test closes the bug.

Stamped a WHOLE marker (SIG_WHOLE='whole', index 3) on baseline cache entries; on_base re-measures only legacy markerless len==LINE_CHARS text. Added test_a_whole_cause_of_exactly_line_chars_is_not_remeasured; legacy test now writes the pre-marker 3-element format raw.

chunk_findings.detail: `known`, `cached_sigs`, and `whole` are three separate reads of the cache file, and the new predicate uses `whole` to cancel a re-measure of a length-`LINE_CHARS` signature. Interleaving: `cache_load` and `cache_signatures` both see a legacy entry `[failed, ts, "A"*240]` (no marker); a concurrent `cache_store` then writes a newer entry for the same id that includes `SIG_WHOLE`; `cache_whole` observes that marker. `len(cached_sigs[i]) == LINE_CHARS and i not in whole` is then false, so the id is dropped from `todo`. The tally keeps the stale 240-character cut text and never re-measures, which is the case the marker was supposed to prevent.

chunk_findings.detail: `cache_store` stamps `SIG_WHOLE` on every non-empty signature (`[f, now, sig, SIG_WHOLE if sig else ""]`) and never checks that the text was kept past `LINE_CHARS`. A caller that still stores a capped reason — the confirmed ERROR path that truncates past 240 — therefore writes a legacy cut as verified-whole. Given `cache_store(..., {"t": True}, sigs={"t": "E"*240})` where the real cause is 300 chars, `cache_snapshot` / `cache_whole` report `t` as whole, so `on_base` skips the re-measure that used to run for an unmarked length-`LINE_CHARS` entry and the tail stays hidden for the TTL.

chunk_findings.detail: `cache_store` still stamps `SIG_WHOLE` on every non-empty signature (`merged[i] = [f, now, sig, SIG_WHOLE if sig else ""]`) and never checks that the text was kept past `LINE_CHARS`. Keeping ERROR reasons whole in `flakes.py` does not answer the probe: `cache_store` is the writer that sets the marker, and it still treats any non-empty string as verified-whole. Given `cache_store(..., {"t": True}, sigs={"t": "E"*240})` where the real cause is 300 characters (or any other caller that still passes a capped reason), `cache_whole` / `cache_snapshot` report `t` as whole, so `on_base` skips the re-measure the marker was added to force.
